intro: This is Harran, an ancient city in Şanlıurfa province with roots in the 3rd millennium BC. It is a city of beehive houses, and home to the first university of the Islamic world.
history: Harran was a centre of the moon-god Sin and a crossroads for caravans. Later it became something new: a hub of medieval astronomy and medicine.
structure-3: Now you are looking at Harran's iconic beehive houses. Their conical mud-brick roofs keep the interiors cool. Step closer and imagine the relief of stepping inside on a hot day.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Mosque and its minaret, Harran Castle and the City gates.
facts: Did you know? The beehive houses are built of mudbrick and stay about 10°C cooler inside. Their conical shape is an architecture for staying cool without electricity, and it has not changed in millennia. Harran is one of the longest continuously inhabited places on earth; in the Book of Genesis, Abraham stayed here with his family. It was the cult centre of the moon god Sin and one of the last places to give up its pagan tradition, and under Islam its school became famous for astronomy and mathematics.
outro: This brings our tour of Harran to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
